name: Portuguese Cistern
hero_subtitle: Columns, vaults and a ray of light on the water — the magic of Mazagan.

overview.title: An underground jewel of light and water
overview.p1: Built in the 16th century by the Portuguese, first as a warehouse or arsenal then converted into a cistern, this underground hall is the highlight of a visit to El Jadida.
overview.p2: Five rows of stone columns support a vaulted ceiling. A thin layer of water covers the floor and reflects the architecture. A circular opening in the ceiling lets a shaft of sunlight in — the effect is striking, especially in the morning.
overview.p3: The cistern has appeared in films and remains one of the most photographed places on Morocco's Atlantic coast. Allow half an hour for the visit and photos.

q1.question: How much time for the cistern?
q1.answer: 30 to 45 minutes is enough for the visit and photos.

q2.question: Is there water on the floor?
q2.answer: Yes, a thin layer reflects the columns — walk carefully.

q3.question: Can I visit with children?
q3.answer: Yes, with supervision because of the wet floor.

q4.question: Is the cistern open every day?
q4.answer: Often closed on Tuesdays; check current hours before you go.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required, but a guide adds historical context to the Portuguese City.
